title: I Took the Viola-da-Gamba Checkout to the Consort Lead Who Left My Numbered Bow

parts.text: I stepped into the consort room at 5:06 p.m. and lead Isolde was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE GAMBA. NINETY MINUTES. BOWS STAY WITH THE CHECKOUT. I was thirty, consort secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered bows. Isolde shrugged. "Leads are the hair." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover rosin on my numbered bow. Then I asked for the bow log. At 5:14 the desk pinged why Isolde's name was on my hair. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Isolde's leftover rosin on my numbered bow.

social.video_title: She left my numbered gamba bow on my checkout — Part 1/2
social.description: Consort room, leftover rosin, a ninety-minute clock she posted. I logged the bow. Would you have asked for the bow log?

parts.text: Isolde called it bowing-in until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the rosin still. The bow went back to my numbered checkout. Isolde ran a slot of her own and told the next lead atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT THE HAIR. I keep my bow on a labeled rack. Isolde brown-bags her bowing-in. The consort room finally looks like a checkout, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Leads are not the hair — Part 2/2
social.description: Bow log, numbered bow, and a second line on the board. Was bowing-in ever my hair?
